definition: A patch lies closer to A if it shows exposed ground, buildings or vegetation rather than extensive bright snow cover. Green vegetation in true color and strong red vegetation in false color support A. Water-only patches are less diagnostic; these A examples look bluer and smoother than the darker, visibly rippled B examples.
cues: Extensive white cover across terrain, remaining white or pale cyan in false color, favors B.
Green vegetation that becomes vivid red in false color favors A.
Clearly exposed fields, streets and roofs with little white ground cover favor A.
For water-only scenes, blue and relatively smooth favors A; darker, more visibly rippled water favors B, weakly.
